Subject: Distribution & connector handoff — initial manifest

Hi Karthik / Camila,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As discussed, we want to move forward with a lightweight distribution arrangement so Redwood can host a non-commercial download/connector for Hydra's open 7B variant while we finalize licensing. Attaching a manifest with checksums and a short readme describing the checkpoint splits and quantization artifacts.

High-level asks from our side:
- Clarify which license variant (attestation vs. full publisher CLA) Redwood requires to expose weights via the hosted connector.
- Minimal embargo/geo restrictions we must respect in your console routing policies.
- Verification steps Redwood will perform when you accept a publisher upload (artifact validation, provenance checks).

We'd appreciate a short mutual action plan and an approximate timeline for a staged rollout (test -> limited customer -> public).

Att: hydra_model_manifest.csv, hydra_weights-readme.txt

Thanks,
Alice Jain
Head of Partnerships, Hydra Labs

Hydra Labs | hydralabs.ai
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Alice Jain <alice@hydralabs.ai>
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 09 Aug 2026 11:03:14 -0700
Subject: Re: Distribution & connector handoff — initial manifest

Alice — thanks for the manifest and the clear list. Quick replies inline and a proposed next-step plan below.

License: we can accept either (a) an attestation + standard publisher addendum, or (b) a signed Publisher CLA for commercial redistribution. For the hosted connector (read-only downloads via signed URLs), attestation + the publisher addendum is typically sufficient for initial exposure; we require a CLA for revenue-sharing or bundling.

Embargo/geo: Redwood can enforce region-based routing. We need a list of restricted territories (if any). Default is global. If you have export control flags on specific models, add them to the manifest as a field we can parse.

Validation: our intake does the following in order:
1) checksum + manifest validation (basic)
2) provenance scan for upstream attributions (open-source origin)
3) optional static scanner for unusual binary blobs (we'll flag and quarantine)

Proposed timeline:
- Day 0: finalize attestation form and upload to staging S3 (you)
- Day 1–2: Redwood intake + automated validation
- Day 3–6: Internal QA and connector compatibility test (we'll run a sample conversion to Redwood loader)
- Week 2: limited partner rollout (select customers)

I'm looping in Camila to confirm clause language and Sergio for rev-share / attribution.

Next steps: please confirm you want (attestation) or (CLA) for the initial rollout and share any embargo list. We'll draft a short mutual action plan doc for signatures.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
From: camila_reyes@redwood.com
To: Alice Jain <alice@hydralabs.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:18:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Distribution & connector handoff — initial manifest

Thanks Karthik / Alice. A few legal/ops items to put on the table from Redwood's side:

1) License granularity — For the attestation route we ask for a one-page publisher attestation: confirms (i) you hold rights to distribute the checkpoint, (ii) there are no encumbrances for non-commercial downloads, and (iii) that attribution terms are as stated in manifest. We'll attach a template.

2) Embargo + security — If any model contains flagged content (privacy-sensitive or export-controlled), we will segregate it into Dedicated/Private channels and not expose via hosted connector. Please mark flags in metadata.

3) Artifact types — the manifest lists a quantized LLAMA-format shard + optimizer state. We need a short compatibility note describing the tokenizer version and any custom ops; otherwise conversion can fail.

4) Redaction & provenance — we will keep a copy in our staging bucket for validation only; we routinely expire staging artifacts after 30 days unless a retention exception is requested. If you need >30 days, please request explicitly.

Attaching: Redwood Publisher Agreement (draft) and attestation template (see att: redwood_publisher_agreement_draft.pdf).

If Hydra prefers attestation first, we can proceed with that and convert artifacts into our accepted loader format. If Hydra wants revenue-sharing or model bundling, we will need the CLA + rev-share schedule. Tagging Sergio for the latter.

Cheers,
Camila Reyes
Senior Director, Publisher Partnerships | Redwood Inference
From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Alice Jain <alice@hydralabs.ai>, camila_reyes@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 11:02:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Distribution & connector handoff — initial manifest

Hi all — quick note on commercial terms and attribution:

- If Hydra wants listing + discoverability in the Redwood catalog with a revenue share, our standard is a 70/30 split (publisher/Redwood) for downloads enabled through the connector, subject to minimums and a locked-in quarter for reporting. We can be flexible on the exact split for strategic partners.

- Attribution: we require a short copy snippet (one-liner) and a link back to Hydra's model page. We also ask for a machine-readable "attribution.json" in the manifest so we can render provenance in the console.

- Security/compliance: for partners requesting up to 100K monthly downloads, we ask for completed SOC-2 evidence or an enterprise agreement. For the initial limited rollout, that is not required.

I'll run a simple rev-share example for projected downloads and share by EOD.

—Sergio Alvarez
Head of Ecosystem, Redwood Inference
